text:
Sam: Quick follow-up from the iterator/resume RFC — we need to converge on a retry policy for paginated/streamed iterators. current note was vague.
Deepa: +1, saw a customer bug where a transient 503 caused full replays and duplicate side-effects. we need clear idempotency surface.
Tony: For context: two modes we support today: page-based (cursor tokens) and stream-based (long-lived websocket / http2). different failure/retry semantics.
Ingrid: Proposal: make resume-on-retry the default for cursor-based (server-provided resume_token), and require explicit idempotency for item-level side-effects.
Sam: Agree about cursor default. For stream-based, we should prefer short reconnect + resume with a per-session resume_id when the backend supports it. if no resume_id -> fall back to restart.
Deepa: How about SDK ergonomics? In Python/TS/Go we should expose a single iterator abstraction with optional config: `resume_on_error`, `max_retries`, `retry_window_ms`. Example: 
```ts
const it = client.listEvents({pageSize: 200, resume_on_error: true, max_retries: 5});
for await (const ev of it) { ... }
```
```py
it = client.list_events(page_size=200, resume_on_error=True, max_retries=5)
for ev in it: ...
```
Ingrid: That shape is nice. caveat: in Go we typically return a channel or an iterator with `Next() (Item, error)`. add `Resume()` on the iterator to let callers attempt manual resume if needed.
Tony: Transport implications: HTTP/1.1 long-poll can't resume cheaply. gRPC or websocket can attach resume metadata/headers to restore KV-cache. we should document per-transport capabilities and have clear fallback rules.
Sam: Agreed. For retry policy, suggest: exponential backoff, but cap total replay window at `retry_window_ms` (default 30s). If the server resume_token age > window, do not resume automatically — surface an ErrStaleCursor.
Deepa: +1. Also add an opt-in `at_least_once` vs `exactly_once` semantics? exactly-once is hard/expensive; prefer `at_least_once` by default with idempotency guidance in docs.
Ingrid: We should also standardize headers: `X-Resume-Token`, `X-Resume-Offset`, `X-Session-Id` so transports can be transport-agnostic when supported.
Tony: One more: retries for write-side effects inside iterator consumers. if user code fails while processing an item and then SDK retries page fetch, we'll re-deliver items. need to call this out. maybe expose a middleware/hook `checkpoint(item_id)` that client code can call to mark progress server-side.
Sam: Good idea. Add a small example in docs showing a checkpoint pattern.
Deepa: Can we add telemetry: when resume happens, emit an event in Console with `resume_type`, `replayed_items`, `transport`. Helps customers debug regressions.
deploy-bot: Deploy scheduled: iterator-retry-policy-v0.1 -> staging at 2024-04-03T14:00:00Z :rocket:
Tony: Next steps: I can draft the API sketches for TS/Python/Go (iterator config + resume API). Ingrid will enumerate transport capability matrix. Deepa will write the docs section on idempotency and checkpointing. Sam will fold into the RFC follow-up doc.
Sam: Thanks — small follow-up: let's add a`resume_on_error: "auto|manual|never"` tri-state so we avoid implicit surprising behavior for critical customers.
Deepa: +1 for tri-state. I'll add examples for each.
Ingrid: I'll map tri-state to transport behavior in matrix (e.g., auto->attempt resume if transport supports `X-Resume-Token` and token age < window).
Tony: I'll include pseudo-code for `Next()` semantics and error classes `ErrStaleCursor`, `ErrResumeUnsupported`.
Sam: Cool. If no objections I'll PR the API doc tomorrow. :thumbsup:
